title: $E_X$ is $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ with $\ell$ inverted
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and $X$ a scheme. Let $\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ denote the colimit,
in sheaves of $\cO_{E,X}$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, of
$$
\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \ell\ }\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \ell\ }\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \ell\ }\cdots,
$$
with its ring structure as the localization of $\cO_{E,X}$ at $\ell$. Then the map
$\varphi\colon\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$ of [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield], together with the maps
$\ell^{-m}\varphi$ on the $m$-th term, induces an isomorphism of sheaves of rings
$$
\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }E_X .
$$
In particular $\ell$ acts invertibly on $E_X$, and $E_X$ is a flat $\cO_{E,X}$-module.

proof.text: *On the point.* Use the section description and absolute value in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and the inclusion of [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point]. For a profinite set $S$ and $h\in C(S,E)$, the nested open subsets $h^{-1}(\{x:|x|<\ell^m\})$, $m\geq0$, cover the compact space $S$: each $|h(s)|$ is a finite real number and $\ell>1$. A finite subcover is contained in its largest member, so $\ell^m h$ takes values in $\cO_E=\{x:|x|\leq1\}$ for some $m$. It is continuous into this subspace. The homomorphisms $q_m:C(S,\cO_E)\to C(S,E)$, $a\mapsto\ell^{-m}a$, satisfy $q_{m+1}(\ell a)=q_m(a)$. They are injective, have nested images, and their images exhaust $C(S,E)$; their union is consequently the sequential colimit of abelian groups. Explicitly, a compatible cocone $(f_m)$ defines the unique map by $\ell^{-m}a\mapsto f_m(a)$; independence follows by passing to a common larger index. Precomposition with $T\to S$ commutes with every $q_m$. The same argument includes $S=\varnothing$.

*The colimit is a sheaf.* The coherent topology in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] is generated by finite jointly surjective families of profinite sets. For such a family, the sheaf condition for abelian groups is the equalizer of the two maps from the finite product of sections on the covering objects to the finite product on their pairwise fibre products. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits], the sectionwise sequential colimit preserves this equalizer. Hence it is a sheaf. Step 1 identifies it naturally with $\underline E$, whose cocone maps are $q_m=\ell^{-m}$ times the inclusion [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point]. The presheaf colimit's universal property also holds among sheaves, since morphisms between sheaves are just morphisms of their underlying presheaves.

source.place: Proof, paragraph '*The colimit is a sheaf.*'

proof.text: *Pullback and module colimit.* By [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], $p_X^*$ is a left adjoint and is strong monoidal. Its colimit preservation follows directly from the adjunction: maps out of $p_X^*\operatorname{colim}F_m$ correspond to compatible maps from $F_m$ into the right adjoint, hence to compatible maps from $p_X^*F_m$. A left adjoint between additive categories preserves zero objects and finite coproducts, hence biproducts and addition of morphisms, so it carries multiplication by the positive integer $\ell$ to multiplication by $\ell$. By [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield], the resulting abelian-sheaf colimit cocone is $\ell^{-m}\varphi:\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$. These maps are $\cO_{E,X}$-linear: on the point this is $(a,b)\mapsto\ell^{-m}ab$, and the strong monoidal functor preserves this identity. This is also a colimit in modules. Indeed, the unique underlying abelian-sheaf factorization $u:E_X\to M$ of any module cocone is linear: compare $u\circ\mu_{E_X}$ and $\mu_M\circ(1\otimes u)$ on $\cO_{E,X}\otimes E_X$. Tensoring abelian sheaves with $\cO_{E,X}$ preserves this colimit by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and the two maps agree on each $\cO_{E,X}\otimes\cO_{E,X}$ by linearity of that cocone. Thus $E_X$ is the displayed sequential module colimit.

*Ring structure and inversion.* The map $\varphi$ is a map of commutative ring objects by [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield]. Multiplication by the constant $1/\ell$ on $\underline E$ is inverse to multiplication by $\ell$; applying the strong monoidal $p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] preserves these identities and makes $\ell$ invertible in $E_X$. By the defining localization universal property, $\varphi$ extends uniquely to a ring map $\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]\to E_X$, sending $a/\ell^m$ to $\ell^{-m}\varphi(a)$. Its underlying module map is exactly the colimit comparison from Step 3, since they agree on every term. It is therefore an isomorphism. In particular this also checks multiplication explicitly: the images of $a/\ell^m$ and $b/\ell^n$ multiply to $\ell^{-(m+n)}\varphi(ab)$.

*Flatness.* Work in the universes and small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] with $\mathcal O=\cO_{E,X}$, with the diagram of Step 3 as degree-zero complexes, and with an arbitrary module $M$ in degree zero. Its tensor-colimit formula gives, naturally in $M$,
$$E_X\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}M\cong\operatorname{colim}_{m\in\mathbf N}(\cO_{E,X}\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}M)\cong\operatorname{colim}(M\xrightarrow{\ell}M\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots).$$
The second identification sends $a\otimes x$ to $ax$ and carries the transition $\ell\otimes1$ to multiplication by $\ell$. A short exact sequence of modules consequently gives a diagram of short exact sequences with these transitions at every index. Exactness of filtered colimits, supplied by the same cited lemma, makes its colimit short exact. Hence $E_X\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}-$ is exact, which is precisely flatness. No quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is used.
